description.narrative:
Young people in marginalized communities most often do not have access to platforms that can positively harness their contribution to community development. The feel invisible, unheard and unappreciated. Their dreams, their potential and their struggles are too often ignored by those in power and decision making positions. Every young person has a voice. It deserves to be heard. And not just a voice, but a big role to play in shaping the development agenda of their communities. According to the Kenya Population and Housing Census 2019, out of the 47.6 million people, 35.7 million of them are aged 35 years and below, representing 75%.
In 2020, UNICEF in collaboration with the African Union Commission and other UN agencies launched the European Union Spotlight Initiative regional Programme for Africa to provide a regional response to addressing sexual gender-based violence, harmful practices and sexual and reproductive health and rights. In 2023, Men End FGM Foundation (MEF) piloted this in West Pokot and Samburu counties, with the aim of capacity building 90 young people to undertake policy and budget advocacy in their respective counties. We focused on advocating for enactment of the county specific Gender Policy and Youth Policy. Additionally, the project engaged young people in institutions of higher learning including TVETs, medical training college and universities across the country under the rallying call #TubongeNaComrades, engaging students on how they can participate in ending harmful practices in their communities, sensitizing them on Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), mental health and drugs and substance abuse.
Building on the successes of the 2023 pilot, this project will engage young people in Samburu county to push for finalization of of the Youth Policy and Gender Policy of the county. Further, we will capacity build the youth in Samburu to undertake budget advocacy by actively participating in budget making process,ensuring that key priority areas affecting them get allocation from the county government. In addition, the project will support sensitization of young people in tertiary institutions within Samburu county on elimination of harmful practices, SRHR and mental health to mark international youth day. They will be trained on media advocacy as well as giving them a platform to engage other youths through periodic X space and webinars, sharing their experiences under this project with the global audience.

participating-org.narrative: Men End FGM Foundation is a global award-winning organization that rallies men and boys to join the quest to eradicate FGM, child marriage and other forms of sexual and gender based violence. The organization's vision is a society free from FGM, child marriage and other forms of sexual and gender-based violence, while its mission is to empower women and girls while keeping men and boys informed through mentorship and awareness creation. Men End FGM believes that achieving gender equality requires inclusive and collaborative efforts. Anchored on this principle, our core values are collaboration, equality, diversity and inclusion, and integrity. Our programmes are diverse, covering women and girls empowerment, engagement of men and boys, youth engagement and inclusion, policy advocacy and promotion of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH). Across all our programmatic areas, promoting gender equality is firmly anchored, a clear manifestation of our believe in multi-sectoral approaches in achieving gender equality.
